note: Selective alpha7 nicotinic agonists normalised sensorimotor gating, social behaviour and recognition memory in rodents and working memory in rhesus at trace doses; AZD0328, TC-5619 and ABT-126 all failed their primary cognition or negative-symptom endpoints in stable schizophrenia.
label: Schizophrenia (alpha7 nAChR)

engagement.model: AstraZeneca trace-dose cognition models: rat PFC dopamine release and operant learning, mouse NOR, rhesus spatial delayed response
engagement.note: Rat microdialysis: trace-dose AZD0328 raised prefrontal dopamine with an inverted dose-effect; no human read-out of this PD marker.
engagement.short: Rat cortical dopamine release, no human read-out
engagement.quote: In vivo microdialysis in awake rats showed an increase in extracellular prefrontal cortical dopamine in response to low doses of AZD0328.
engagement.reason: PD marker never measured in humans
engagement.judgement: The model's PD read-outs (cortical dopamine release; ex-vivo alpha7 up-regulation in Werkheiser 2011, 10.1016/j.neuroscience.2011.04.033) have no human counterpart; the patient study NCT00669903 measured cognition only, which is efficacy, not engagement.

engagement.model: Rodent schizophrenia screens: th(tk-)/th(tk-) mouse PPI and social behaviour, rat apomorphine-PPI, rat novel object recognition
engagement.note: PPI normalisation in th(tk-)/th(tk-) mice was the gating read-out; no P50/PPI measurement with TC-5619, ABT-126 or AZD0328 in patients was found.
engagement.short: Rodent PPI gating, no patient gating data
engagement.quote: At the 0.3 mg/kg dose, there was a statistically significant drug × genotype interaction effect (p = 0.022) demonstrating the ability of TC-5619 to normalize PPI in th(tk−)/th(tk−) mice.
engagement.reason: Gating read-out not taken in patients
engagement.judgement: Human P50 gating data for alpha7 agonists exist only for DMXB-A (GTS-21), which is not a member of this class, so they cannot score here; Hashimoto 2015 (review) lists no gating study for the three members.

engagement.note: Pig PET built after the failures: TC-5619 blocked ~40% of alpha7 binding; no human occupancy for any member exists to compare.
engagement.short: Pig PET occupancy, no human occupancy
engagement.quote: This study underscores the importance of preclinical PET imaging and target engagement analysis in informing clinical trial strategies, including dosing decisions.
engagement.judgement: A post-hoc occupancy model (2024) with no human occupancy datum for TC-5619, ABT-126 or AZD0328; it is a model that exists and was never compared, not a retrodiction, because it reproduces no human result.

dose.confidence_note: Dose-response data not shown in the paper.
dose.model: Rodent schizophrenia screens: th(tk-)/th(tk-) mouse PPI and social behaviour, rat apomorphine-PPI, rat novel object recognition
dose.note: Minimum effective oral dose for recognition memory set at 0.3 mg/kg in rats; PPI and social effects at 0.3 mg/kg; no exposure target stated.
dose.quote: In the dose–response study, the minimum effective dose to produce cognitive-enhancing activity was determined to be 0.3 mg/kg (data not shown).

dose.model: AstraZeneca trace-dose cognition models: rat PFC dopamine release and operant learning, mouse NOR, rhesus spatial delayed response
dose.note: Model predicted efficacy at trace doses (0.00178 mg/kg mouse; 0.00048–0.0016 mg/kg rhesus) with an inverted-U and impairment at 0.48 mg/kg.
dose.quote: Compound-stimulated dopamine release showed an inverted dose effect relation that was maximal at the lowest dose tested (0.00178 mg/kg).
dose.judgement: Castner 2011 (10.1016/j.biopsych.2010.08.006, epub 2010-10) titrated the rhesus dose from the rodent range and found working-memory gains at 0.0016 and 0.00048 mg/kg; that paper defines the human target but appeared after the trial posted.

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; no PK in the abstract and NCT01003379 has no posted results. 'Reached' is mg/kg arithmetic, not a stated exposure target.
dose.model: Rodent schizophrenia screens: th(tk-)/th(tk-) mouse PPI and social behaviour, rat apomorphine-PPI, rat novel object recognition
dose.note: TC-5619 titrated 1→25 mg/day (about 0.35 mg/kg at the top), on the rat 0.3 mg/kg minimum; the exploratory primary endpoint favoured drug.
dose.short: Rat-effective dose range reached, signal seen
dose.quote: GMLT statistically favored TC-5619 (P=0.036) in this exploratory trial.
dose.judgement: Scored same because the trial dosed through the rat-effective range and its primary endpoint responded; it is provisional, as the 2015 phase 2 at 5 and 50 mg reversed it.

efficacy.model: Rodent schizophrenia screens: th(tk-)/th(tk-) mouse PPI and social behaviour, rat apomorphine-PPI, rat novel object recognition
efficacy.note: TC-5619 corrected PPI and social deficits in th(tk-)/th(tk-) mice, reversed apomorphine-PPI deficits and enhanced novel object recognition in rats.
efficacy.short: Rodent positive, negative and cognitive screens positive
efficacy.quote: In these mice TC-5619 acted both alone and synergistically with the antipsychotic clozapine to correct impaired pre-pulse inhibition (PPI) and social behavior which model positive and negative symptoms, respectively.

efficacy.model: AstraZeneca trace-dose cognition models: rat PFC dopamine release and operant learning, mouse NOR, rhesus spatial delayed response
efficacy.note: AZD0328 improved mouse novel object recognition and rat operant learning at trace doses; rhesus working memory followed in 2010.
efficacy.short: Rodent and rhesus cognition improved at trace doses
efficacy.quote: AZD0328 improved novel object recognition in mice over a broad range of doses (0.00178-1.78 mg/kg) and the compound effect was found to be absent in homozygous alpha7 KO animals.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction of change in a cognition composite vs placebo
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry record carries LS means but no p-values; no journal publication of this trial was found.
efficacy.model: AstraZeneca trace-dose cognition models: rat PFC dopamine release and operant learning, mouse NOR, rhesus spatial delayed response
efficacy.note: Phase 2a in 100 stable patients: day-14 CogState GMLT+OCLT composite 0.234/0.240/0.194 vs placebo 0.266 across three dose tiers; terminated.
efficacy.short: Patient cognition composite flat, programme stopped
efficacy.quote: Since AZD0328 is unlikely to meet the current Target Product Profile, Astrazeneca decided to stop further development of AZD0328

patient_trials.quote: Since AZD0328 is unlikely to meet the current Target Product Profile, Astrazeneca decided to stop further development of AZD0328

efficacy.reason: Trace-dose cognition gain absent in patients
efficacy.judgement: Call: the registry is the only patient record; all three AZD0328 arms sat below placebo on the primary composite and the sponsor's stated reason for stopping was failure to meet the target profile. Castner 2011 was published two months after the results posted, so the pairing is dated by the registry with Sydserff 2009 as the public model side at that date.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction of executive-function and SANS change vs placebo
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; NCT01003379 has no posted results; Mazurov 2012 (10.1021/jm301048a) states the animal-to-clinic match in one sentence but exceeds the 40-word quote limit.
efficacy.model: Rodent schizophrenia screens: th(tk-)/th(tk-) mouse PPI and social behaviour, rat apomorphine-PPI, rat novel object recognition
efficacy.note: Exploratory 12-week trial (n=185): primary GMLT favoured TC-5619 (P=0.036) and SANS too (P=0.030), mainly in tobacco users.
efficacy.short: Exploratory trial: primary endpoint favoured drug
efficacy.quote: GMLT statistically favored TC-5619 (P=0.036) in this exploratory trial.

patient_trials.quote: GMLT statistically favored TC-5619 (P=0.036) in this exploratory trial.

efficacy.judgement: Scored same on the primary endpoint of an exploratory trial with a P=0.036 result and no multiplicity control; the same track turns contra in 2015.

efficacy.model: Sub-chronic PCP mouse nest-building / social interaction (Lundbeck back-translation)
efficacy.note: Lundbeck built the PCP nest-building assay as a back-translation of the reported TC-5619/EVP-6124 negative-symptom signal; both reversed the deficit, risperidone did not.
efficacy.quote: Sub-chronic PCP treatment resulted in a significant nest building deficit in mice and treatment with EVP-6124 and TC-5619 reversed this PCP-induced deficit.
efficacy.judgement: A retrodiction by definition: the paper says the drugs were chosen because they 'were reported to exert some beneficial effect on negative symptoms', so the model was validated against the Lieberman 2013 SANS signal, not predictive of it. EVP-6124 is not a member and does not score; TC-5619 does.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction of SANS and cognition change vs placebo
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Walling; NCT01488929 has no posted results.
efficacy.model: Rodent schizophrenia screens: th(tk-)/th(tk-) mouse PPI and social behaviour, rat apomorphine-PPI, rat novel object recognition
efficacy.note: 24-week phase 2 (n=477): SANS primary and all cognitive secondaries negative at 5 and 50 mg; TC-5619 development ended.
efficacy.short: Phase 2 negative on SANS and cognition
efficacy.quote: These results do not support a benefit of TC-5619 for negative or cognitive symptoms in schizophrenia.

patient_trials.quote: SANS score showed no statistical benefit for TC-5619 vs placebo at week 24 (5 mg, 2-tailed P = .159; 50 mg, P = .689).

efficacy.judgement: Call: the rodent screens predicted benefit across positive, negative and cognitive domains; the adequately powered trial found none on its primary (negative symptoms) or on cognition, so the 2012 same is overturned. Dated 2015 by online publication (June 2015; print 2016).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction of SANS change vs placebo
efficacy.confidence_note: The phase 2 began (Dec 2011) before the model paper (2014), but its result was public only after it, so it is the model's first prospective comparison under decision 10.
efficacy.model: Sub-chronic PCP mouse nest-building / social interaction (Lundbeck back-translation)
efficacy.note: The model's first prospective test: TC-5619 did not improve SANS at 5 or 50 mg over 24 weeks.
efficacy.quote: These results do not support a benefit of TC-5619 for negative or cognitive symptoms in schizophrenia.
efficacy.judgement: Decision 10: a retrodiction's first prospective comparison is scored as usual; the model predicted a negative-symptom benefit for TC-5619 that the SANS primary did not show.

efficacy.confidence_note: ABT-126 was never reported in Hauser's models; its own preclinical efficacy work is unpublished (only abuse-liability and MPTP-monkey papers exist), so it enters this track as a sibling drug.
efficacy.model: Rodent schizophrenia screens: th(tk-)/th(tk-) mouse PPI and social behaviour, rat apomorphine-PPI, rat novel object recognition
efficacy.note: ABT-126 phase 2b in nonsmokers (n=432): MCCB +2.66 vs +2.46 placebo at 50 mg; smokers' study (2018) and the 2016 phase 2 also missed.
efficacy.quote: ABT-126 did not demonstrate a consistent effect on cognition in nonsmoking subjects with schizophrenia; however, a trend toward an effect was observed on negative symptoms.

patient_trials.quote: No statistically significant differences were observed in either the change from baseline for the MCCB neurocognitive composite score (+2.66 [±0.54] for ABT-126 50 mg vs +2.46 [±0.56] for placebo at week 12; P>0.05) or the UPSA-2ER.

ABT-126 showed an improvement that fell short of significance on the MCCB composite score at week 12 (least squares mean difference from placebo, 1.3 and 1.5 for the 10 mg and 25 mg groups, respectively).
ABT-126 did not demonstrate a procognitive effect in subjects with stable schizophrenia who smoke.

efficacy.reason: Three drugs, no primary endpoint met
efficacy.judgement: Strengthens the 2015 contra with a second member: Haig 2016 AJP (phase 2, 10/25 mg) fell short on MCCB with a nonsmoker subgroup signal that the 432-patient nonsmoker phase 2b then failed to confirm; the extension NCT01834638 was terminated because 'Study endpoint in preceding base study M10-855 not met.' Encenicline is excluded as a non-member.

safety.model: Rodent schizophrenia screens: th(tk-)/th(tk-) mouse PPI and social behaviour, rat apomorphine-PPI, rat novel object recognition
safety.note: Selectivity screen (no muscle or ganglionic nAChR activity) led the authors to predict low potential for nicotinic side effects.
safety.quote: The lack of interaction with muscle and ganglionic-type receptors suggests low potential for nicotinic side effects with TC-5619.

safety.model: AstraZeneca trace-dose cognition models: rat PFC dopamine release and operant learning, mouse NOR, rhesus spatial delayed response
safety.note: Rhesus predicted cognitive impairment at 0.48 mg/kg, 300× the effective dose; patient dosing stayed 50× below it, so the harm was never tested.
safety.quote: Acute AZD0328 improved cognitive performance when the dose was titrated down to .0016 and .00048 mg/kg from a cognitively impairing dose of .48 mg/kg.
safety.reason: Predicted harm outside the dosed range
safety.judgement: The registry lists dyspepsia (9/23, 10/37, 5/18 vs 4/22) and nausea (4/18 high dose vs 0) above placebo, but the model made no GI prediction and a rhesus working-memory task cannot show dyspepsia, so its silence is not a miss.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Walling 2016: 'TC-5619 was generally well tolerated.' Haig 2018: constipation 5.8% vs 0% on ABT-126; AZD0328 registry shows dyspepsia above placebo; none was called a safety signal.
safety.model: Rodent schizophrenia screens: th(tk-)/th(tk-) mouse PPI and social behaviour, rat apomorphine-PPI, rat novel object recognition
safety.note: 12-week trial: no clinically noteworthy safety findings; the 24-week phase 2 (2015) and ABT-126 trials also reported tolerability like placebo.
safety.short: Well tolerated, as the selectivity screen predicted
safety.quote: TC-5619 was generally well tolerated with no clinically noteworthy safety findings.
safety.reason: Tolerability prediction held in three trials
safety.judgement: Call: the model's stated prediction (no peripheral nicotinic harms) held; GI complaints (constipation with ABT-126, dyspepsia with AZD0328) were mild, not nicotinic in the muscle/ganglionic sense the paper meant, and no trial reported a safety concern. A reader who treats constipation 5.8% vs 0% as a contradicted silence could score contra; rodents could in principle show GI motility effects, which were not reported.
